$meta.purpose: Manufacturer-recommended installation tools for residential solar RACKING/structural work (rail cutting, torque, roof attachment, safety, sealant). Drives the 'Suggested Tools' section of the job BOM.
primarySources: IronRidge XR Flush Mount Installation Manual v5.2, 2026 (files.ironridge.com/pitched-roof-mounting/resources/brochures/IronRidge_Flush_Mount_Installation_Manual.pdf) — TOOLS REQUIRED + BONDING HARDWARE TORQUE VALUES pages, full text extracted

Roof Tech RT-MINI II Installation Manual, Jun/2025 (design.roof-tech.us/PDF/Installation-Manuals/Installation-Manual-RT-MINI-II.pdf) — 'Tools Required for Assembly' p.3 + Technical Note, full text extracted
Unirac SolarMount Installation Guide (ressupply.com/documents/unirac/SolarMount_Installation_Manual.pdf, mirrors unirac.com) — 'Wrenches and Torque' tables + install steps, full text extracted

SnapNrack Ultra Rail Installation Manual v4.6.1 (ressupply.com/documents/snapnrack/Ultra_Rail_Installation_Manual.pdf) — per-section 'Required Tools' lists + Hardware Torque Specifications table + Rail Finishing section, full text extracted
K2 Systems CrossRail Assembly Instructions US (k2-systems.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/CrossRail-AI-US.pdf) — tools overview + clamp torques (via search excerpts, not full-text verified)

$meta.extractionNote: IronRidge, Roof Tech, Unirac, SnapNrack values quoted from full manual text extracted via pdftotext on 2026-07-11. K2 values from search excerpts of the official AI-US PDF — verify before printing on a customer-facing document.

general.tool: Portable band saw (deep-cut, with non-ferrous/fine-tooth blade)
general.use: Cutting aluminum rail to length, on the roof or at the cut station
general.why: Preferred by installers for rail: cold cut, clean edge, minimal burr, no hot chips or sparks landing on shingles (unlike an abrasive saw). SnapNrack's Rail Finishing section explicitly lists 'Reciprocating Saw or Portable Band Saw' as the required cutting tool.
general.source: SnapNrack Ultra Rail Installation Manual v4.6.1, Rail Finishing section ('Required Tools: Reciprocating Saw or Portable Band Saw'); installer best-practice guides (e.g. portaband.com pro tips, gogreensolar DIY installer tool list)

general.tool: Miter/chop saw with non-ferrous carbide blade (triple-chip grind, negative rake)
general.use: Ground-level rail cut station when many rails must be cut square and fast
general.why: Acceptable alternative to a bandsaw for aluminum extrusion IF fitted with a blade rated for non-ferrous metal; clamp the rail. Keep it on the ground — it throws chips. Never use an abrasive metal-cutoff wheel on structural aluminum rail.
general.source: SnapNrack Ultra Rail Manual Wire Management section lists 'Reciprocating Saw or Chop Saw' for cutting rail cover; blade guidance from The Fabricator, 'Tips to successfully saw and select blades for nonferrous materials'

general.tool: Deburring tool and/or flat metal file
general.use: Remove sharp edges from every field-cut rail end before installing end caps/end clamps
general.why: SnapNrack rail-cut instructions: 'remove any sharp edges' after cutting. Burrs cut hands and wire insulation and can interfere with end-cap seating.
general.source: SnapNrack Ultra Rail Installation Manual v4.6.1, Rail Finishing installation instructions steps 2-3

general.use: Final torque on ALL racking structural + bonding hardware
general.why: IronRidge lists 'Torque Wrench (0-300 in-lbs)' in TOOLS REQUIRED; every major racking manual (Unirac, SnapNrack, K2, Roof Tech) requires torqued fasteners because clamp bonding (UL 2703) is torque-dependent. Most racking specs are 60-300 in-lbs, so an inch-pound wrench is the right range; a 3/8-drive ft-lb wrench works for the 25-30 ft-lb items.
general.source: IronRidge XR Flush Mount Installation Manual v5.2, TOOLS REQUIRED; Unirac SolarMount Installation Guide 'Wrenches and Torque'; SnapNrack Ultra Rail Manual required tools

general.use: Drill: pilot holes and general fastening. Impact driver: driving structural lag bolts ONLY
general.why: IronRidge's tool list is explicit: 'Cordless Drill (non-impact)' plus 'Impact Driver (for lag bolts)'. Do NOT use the impact on clamp/bonding hardware (over-torques, wrecks UL 2703 bond) and never on Roof Tech M5 screws (manual prohibits it).
general.source: IronRidge XR Flush Mount Installation Manual v5.2, TOOLS REQUIRED; Roof Tech RT-MINI II Manual Technical Note ('avoid the use of an impact driver')

general.tool: Stud finder (deep-scan) or hammer for sounding, + tape measure
general.use: Locating rafters/trusses before drilling attachment pilot holes
general.why: SnapNrack lists 'Hammer or Stud Finder' as a required tool in every roof-attachment section. Confirm spacing with a tape from a known rafter (eave/gable end); verify with the pilot hole — 'If the roof framing member is not found then seal the pilot hole immediately with roofing sealant.'
general.source: SnapNrack Ultra Rail Installation Manual v4.6.1, Required Tools + Installation Note; IronRidge XR Flush Mount Manual ('locate a rafter, drill a pilot hole and install the attachment')

general.use: Marking rafter lines and transferring rail/attachment layout onto the roof
general.why: 'Transfer rail locations using a chalk line' (SnapNrack); Roof Tech requires a chalk line to align RT-MINI II bases on the rafter; IronRidge HUG aligns to a chalk line.
general.source: SnapNrack Ultra Rail Manual System Layout; Roof Tech RT-MINI II Manual Tools Required + Bracket Installation; IronRidge XR Flush Mount Manual (HUG install)

general.tool: Pilot drill bits — size per attachment manufacturer (3/16" SnapNrack & Unirac lags; 1/4" IronRidge FlashFoot2; 7/32" IronRidge QBase/GF-1)
general.use: Pilot holes into rafters for 5/16" lag screws / attachment hardware
general.why: Each manual specifies its own pilot size — do not generalize across brands. Back-fill every pilot hole with roofing sealant before setting the lag (all manuals).
general.source: SnapNrack Ultra Rail Manual ('Drill with 3/16" Pilot Drill Bit'); Unirac SolarMount Guide (3/16" pilot holes for SolarHook lags); IronRidge XR Flush Mount Manual v5.2 (FlashFoot2: 'Drill 1/4" pilot holes'; QBase/GF-1: '7/32" drill bit')

general.use: Back-filling pilot holes, sealing missed/abandoned holes, optional UV top-coat on flashings
general.why: Every attachment manual requires sealant in the pilot hole; SnapNrack: 'All missed pilot holes should be sealed immediately.' Roof Tech publishes an approved-sealant list (see byBrand).
general.source: SnapNrack Ultra Rail Manual; IronRidge XR Flush Mount Manual ('back fill with roofing manufacturers' approved sealant'); Roof Tech RT-MINI II Manual

general.use: Lifting shingle courses to slide flashings into place without tearing shingles
general.why: Listed as a required tool in SnapNrack's comp-shingle attachment sections.
general.source: SnapNrack Ultra Rail Installation Manual v4.6.1, Required Tools

general.use: Stainless racking hardware threads (where the manual says to apply)
general.why: Stainless hardware galls. Unirac: 'Apply minimal lubricant to bolts... preferably Anti-Seize' (factory-applied on mid-clamp bolts; NOT used on Pro-series 11 ft-lb clamps or rail splices). Roof Tech 'recommends all stainless steel threads be lubricated.'
general.source: Unirac SolarMount Installation Guide, Wrenches and Torque notes; Roof Tech RT-MINI II Manual Technical Note

general.tool: Personal fall arrest system: full-body harness + roof anchor (5,000 lb rated) + SRL or rope grab/lifeline
general.use: Fall protection for all roof work at 6 ft or more above lower level
general.why: OSHA residential construction rule: guardrails, safety nets, or PFAS required at 6+ ft; anchorage must support 5,000 lbs per attached worker (29 CFR 1926.502). SnapNrack manual: 'Appropriate fall protection or prevention gear should be used.'
general.source: OSHA Fall Protection in Residential Construction fact sheet; osha.gov/green-jobs/solar/falls; 29 CFR 1926.502; SnapNrack Ultra Rail Manual Safety Guidance

general.why: 'Use appropriate ladder safety equipment when accessing the roof from ground level' — SnapNrack Safety Guidance.
general.source: SnapNrack Ultra Rail Installation Manual v4.6.1, Safety Guidance

general.tool: Module handling: 2-person carry (standard); optional module hoist/ladder lift for getting panels to the roof
general.use: Moving 60-75 lb modules to and across the roof
general.why: Two-person handling is standard industry practice for residential modules; powered vacuum lifters are a commercial/large-crew option, not required by any residential racking manual. Panel manufacturers prohibit carrying modules by the junction box or cables.
general.source: Industry best practice; no residential racking manual mandates a lifting device (verified against IronRidge/Roof Tech/Unirac/SnapNrack tool lists)

general.use: Staging modules and rail on the roof without scuffing shingles or module glass; kneeling pad on hot shingles
general.why: Common installer practice to protect shingles and module edges during staging. Not a manufacturer requirement — quality-of-install item.
general.source: Installer best practice (not in manufacturer tool lists)

general.use: All cutting, drilling, and hardware work
general.why: 'Always wear proper eye protection' — SnapNrack Safety Guidance. Cut aluminum edges are sharp until deburred.
general.source: SnapNrack Ultra Rail Installation Manual v4.6.1, Safety Guidance

caveats: Torque values are REVISION-SPECIFIC. Always use the manual revision shipped with the product: e.g. IronRidge UFO clamp = 80 in-lbs in XR Flush Mount Manual v5.2 (2026) but 84 in-lbs in older revisions. Do not print a torque on the BOM without the manual version note.

Roof Tech M5 wood screws deliberately have NO numeric torque — spec is 'tighten until the conical washer stops rotating'; torque varies with wood condition. Do not invent a ft-lb number for them, and flag that impact drivers are prohibited on these screws.
K2 Systems values here came from search excerpts of the official CrossRail AI-US PDF, not a full-text extraction — field-verify against the current manual (k2-systems.com) before relying on them.

SnapNrack torque table was extracted from a PDF whose column alignment shifts; the three headline rows (Ultra clamps 16 ft-lbs, splice/L-foot 12 ft-lbs, legacy clamps 10 ft-lbs) were cross-checked against SnapNrack training guide excerpts, but verify lug/MLPE rows against the live manual before printing.

Lag-bolt pilot bit sizes are per-manufacturer, NOT a universal rule: 3/16" (SnapNrack, Unirac SolarHook), 1/4" (IronRidge FlashFoot2), 7/32" (IronRidge QBase/GF-1). Some manuals (Unirac) defer lag size/embedment to the project engineering — the BOM should show the attachment brand's number.
Lag bolts generally have NO published torque (IronRidge/SnapNrack say 'fully seat' / 'minimum 2.5" embedment') because torque-to-clamp in wood varies; do not list a lag torque value.

Anti-seize is conditional: Unirac requires it on some hardware (mid clamps) and forbids it on others (Pro clamps 11 ft-lbs, splices) — torque specs change meaning with lubrication, so pair each torque with its anti-seize note.

No residential racking manufacturer requires a vacuum module lifter; 2-person carry plus optional ladder hoist is the standard. Vacuum lifters are listed as optional handling equipment only — no part numbers included by design.

Rail cutting: manufacturer manuals name the tool class (SnapNrack: 'Reciprocating Saw or Portable Band Saw') but the bandsaw-over-chopsaw preference (cold cut, no hot chips on shingles) is installer best practice, not a manual mandate. Abrasive cutoff wheels on structural rail are universally discouraged.

IronRidge tool list distinguishes 'Cordless Drill (non-impact)' from 'Impact Driver (for lag bolts)' — the impact is ONLY for lags; using it on clamp/bonding hardware can over-torque and void the UL 2703 bonding certification assumptions.

OSHA fall-protection items (harness, 5,000-lb anchor, SRL) are legal requirements at 6+ ft in residential construction (29 CFR 1926.501/502), not manufacturer suggestions — treat as mandatory on the BOM, not 'suggested'.
